required_actions: Open Settings, tap Accessibility, then tap Magnification (critical)
Turn on the Magnification shortcut (critical)
Start magnification with the shortcut (critical)
Tap anywhere except the keyboard or navigation bar to turn on full-screen zoom (critical)
Pinch with two fingers to zoom (critical)
Drag with two fingers to move around the screen (critical)
Use the shortcut again to stop (non-critical)
In the Find My app, go to the Devices tab (critical)
Scroll down and select the missing iPhone (critical)
Tap More (critical)
Scroll down and turn on Lost Mode (critical)
Tap Activate (critical)
Follow the onscreen steps to show contact information (optional; the page says this step is optional)

Computer route: go to icloud.com/find, sign in, select Find Devices if a verification code is asked for, select the iPhone under All Devices, then play a sound or mark it as lost (critical for that route)
reasons: S5 = 1: 'Lost Mode' (step 4) and 'Family Sharing group' (parenthetical after step 2) are used without any explanation, which a low-confidence user cannot act on. Also step 5 presents the optional contact-information step ('if you want to display your contact information') as a required step ('Follow the steps on the screen to add a phone number and a message'). This is the final re-review, so the example cannot be revised further.

required_actions: On another Android phone, open the Find Hub app, or on a browser go to google.com/android/find (critical)
Sign in (critical)
Select the lost phone from the listed devices (critical)
If asked, enter the lock screen PIN; if the phone has no PIN or runs Android 8 or lower, enter the Google password (conditional)
Read the device's location on the map after selecting it (page: 'On the map, you get information about the device's location') (non-critical)
Play sound: rings at full volume for 5 minutes, even on silent or vibrate (non-critical)
Mark as lost: tap Mark as lost, then Next, add contact info and a message, then tap Mark as lost to confirm (non-critical)
Factory reset: permanently deletes data, and the phone is no longer available in Find Hub afterward (non-critical)
reasons: S1 = 1 and S4 = 1: the Find Hub page says 'On the map, you get information about the device's location', but the reply never tells the user that the location appears on a map after the phone is selected. The round-2 writer removed the map sentence on the basis that the page did not describe a map; that was a misreading. Without it, the user does not know what they will see, which is the core outcome of finding the phone. The other claims check out: 'If its current location can't be found, you may still see its last known location, if available' matches the page's last-known-location sentence, 'Add a message and a phone number' is consistent with the page's lock-screen phone number statement, and 'afterward you can't find it with Find Hub' matches 'When you factory reset a device, it will no longer be available in Find Hub.' This is the final re-review, so the example cannot be revised further.
